subject: science
chapter_title: The Invisible Living World - Beyond Our Naked Eye

concepts.title: Introduction to Microorganisms
concepts.definition: Microorganisms are living things so small that they can be seen only through a microscope; they include bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoa, and algae.
concepts.key_idea: Microorganisms live all around us and inside us, though they are too small to see with the naked eye.
question_patterns: What are microorganisms?
Name four types of microorganisms.
Why are microorganisms called invisible living things?
Where do microorganisms live?
How can we see microorganisms?

solution_steps.explain: State that microorganisms are living things too small to see without a microscope.
Name the main groups such as bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoa, and algae.
Mention that they live in air, water, soil, and inside other organisms.

worked_examples.question: What are microorganisms?
worked_examples.solution: Microorganisms are living things so small that they can be seen only through a microscope.
worked_examples.answer: Living things visible only through a microscope.

worked_examples.question: Name four types of microorganisms.
worked_examples.solution: Four types are bacteria, viruses, fungi, and protozoa.
worked_examples.answer: Bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoa.

worked_examples.question: How can we see microorganisms?
worked_examples.solution: We can see microorganisms using a microscope, which magnifies them many times.
worked_examples.answer: By using a microscope.

exercises.question: Why are microorganisms called invisible living things?

concepts.title: Classification of Microorganisms
concepts.definition: Microorganisms are classified into groups such as bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoa, and algae based on their structure, size, and way of life.
concepts.key_idea: Different groups of microorganisms differ in structure, size, and how they live and reproduce.
question_patterns: On what basis are microorganisms classified?
How are bacteria different from viruses?
What is the difference between protozoa and algae?
Name one characteristic of fungi.
Which microorganisms have a cell wall but no nucleus?

solution_steps.explain: Note which group of microorganisms the question is about.
Describe the structure, size, and way of life of that group.
Explain how it differs from another group if the question asks for a comparison.

worked_examples.question: On what basis are microorganisms classified?
worked_examples.solution: Microorganisms are classified based on their structure, size, and way of life.
worked_examples.answer: Structure, size, and way of life.

worked_examples.question: How are bacteria different from viruses?
worked_examples.solution: Bacteria are single-celled living organisms that can survive on their own, while viruses need a host cell to reproduce.
worked_examples.answer: Bacteria are living single cells; viruses need a host to reproduce.

worked_examples.question: Name one characteristic of fungi.
worked_examples.solution: Fungi are organisms that feed on dead or decaying matter and include moulds and yeast.
worked_examples.answer: Fungi feed on dead or decaying matter; examples are mould and yeast.

exercises.question: What is the difference between protozoa and algae?
Which microorganisms have a cell wall but no nucleus?
Give one example of each main group of microorganisms.

concepts.title: Useful Microorganisms in Food
concepts.definition: Some microorganisms such as yeast and lactobacillus are useful in making foods like bread, curd, cheese, and dosa by fermentation.
concepts.key_idea: Friendly microorganisms help prepare and preserve many everyday foods through fermentation.
question_patterns: Which microorganism is used to make bread?
How is curd formed from milk?
Name one food made using yeast.
What role does lactobacillus play in curd formation?
Give one example of fermentation in food preparation.

solution_steps.explain: Note which food product is being prepared.
State which microorganism is involved in the process.
Describe how the microorganism changes the food, such as by fermentation.

worked_examples.question: Which microorganism is used to make bread?
worked_examples.solution: Yeast is used to make bread because it produces carbon dioxide gas that makes the dough rise.
worked_examples.answer: Yeast makes bread rise by producing carbon dioxide.

worked_examples.question: How is curd formed from milk?
worked_examples.solution: Lactobacillus bacteria convert the sugar in milk into lactic acid, which turns milk into curd.
worked_examples.answer: Lactobacillus converts milk sugar into lactic acid to form curd.

worked_examples.question: Name one food made using yeast.
worked_examples.solution: Dosa batter is made using yeast, which ferments the rice and lentil mixture.
worked_examples.answer: Dosa is made using yeast fermentation.

exercises.question: What role does lactobacillus play in curd formation?
Give one example of fermentation in food preparation.
Name one food preserved using microorganisms.

concepts.title: Useful Microorganisms in Medicine and Environment
concepts.definition: Microorganisms are used to make medicines such as antibiotics and vaccines, and they help the environment by decomposing waste and fixing nitrogen in soil.
concepts.key_idea: Microorganisms protect health through medicines and keep the environment clean by decomposing waste.
question_patterns: Which microorganism produces antibiotics?
How do microorganisms help the environment?
What is the role of bacteria in soil fertility?
Name one medicine made using microorganisms.
How do microorganisms decompose waste?

solution_steps.explain: Decide whether the question is about medicine or the environment.
Name the microorganism involved, such as penicillium for penicillin.
Describe how the microorganism helps, such as killing bacteria or decomposing waste.

worked_examples.question: Which microorganism produces antibiotics?
worked_examples.solution: The fungus penicillium produces the antibiotic penicillin, which kills harmful bacteria.
worked_examples.answer: Penicillium produces penicillin.

worked_examples.question: How do microorganisms help the environment?
worked_examples.solution: Microorganisms decompose dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the soil.
worked_examples.answer: They decompose dead matter and return nutrients to soil.

worked_examples.question: What is the role of bacteria in soil fertility?
worked_examples.solution: Rhizobium bacteria fix nitrogen from the air into the soil, making it fertile for plants.
worked_examples.answer: Rhizobium fixes nitrogen in soil to improve fertility.

exercises.question: Name one medicine made using microorganisms.
How do microorganisms decompose waste?
Give one example of bacteria improving soil.

concepts.title: Harmful Microorganisms and Disease
concepts.definition: Some microorganisms are harmful because they cause diseases in humans, animals, and plants; these are called pathogens.
concepts.key_idea: Pathogenic microorganisms enter the body and cause diseases, so hygiene and prevention are important.
question_patterns: What are pathogens?
Name one disease caused by bacteria.
How do microorganisms cause disease?
Name one disease caused by a virus.
How can we prevent the spread of harmful microorganisms?

solution_steps.explain: Note whether the disease is caused by a bacterium, virus, protozoan, or fungus.
Describe how the pathogen enters the body, such as through air, water, or food.
Mention hygiene, vaccination, or clean water to prevent the disease.

worked_examples.question: What are pathogens?
worked_examples.solution: Pathogens are disease-causing microorganisms such as certain bacteria and viruses.
worked_examples.answer: Disease-causing microorganisms.

worked_examples.question: Name one disease caused by bacteria.
worked_examples.solution: Tuberculosis is caused by the bacterium Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
worked_examples.answer: Tuberculosis is caused by bacteria.

worked_examples.question: Name one disease caused by a virus.
worked_examples.solution: Influenza, or flu, is caused by a virus.
worked_examples.answer: Flu is caused by a virus.

exercises.question: How do microorganisms cause disease?
How can we prevent the spread of harmful microorganisms?
Name one disease caused by a protozoan.

concepts.title: The Nitrogen Cycle and Microorganisms
concepts.definition: The nitrogen cycle is the movement of nitrogen between the air, soil, and living things, with microorganisms playing key roles in fixing, converting, and releasing nitrogen.
concepts.key_idea: Microorganisms such as rhizobium and denitrifying bacteria keep nitrogen cycling between air, soil, and organisms.
question_patterns: What is the nitrogen cycle?
Which microorganism fixes nitrogen in the soil?
How do microorganisms help in the nitrogen cycle?
What is nitrogen fixation?
How does nitrogen return to the air from the soil?

solution_steps.explain: Note which part of the nitrogen cycle is involved, such as fixation or denitrification.
Name the microorganism involved, such as rhizobium for fixation.
Describe how the microorganism converts nitrogen from one form to another.

worked_examples.question: What is the nitrogen cycle?
worked_examples.solution: The nitrogen cycle is the movement of nitrogen between the air, soil, and living things with the help of microorganisms.
worked_examples.answer: Movement of nitrogen between air, soil, and living things.

worked_examples.question: Which microorganism fixes nitrogen in the soil?
worked_examples.solution: Rhizobium bacteria, found in the roots of leguminous plants, fix nitrogen from the air into the soil.
worked_examples.answer: Rhizobium fixes nitrogen in the soil.

worked_examples.question: How does nitrogen return to the air from the soil?
worked_examples.solution: Denitrifying bacteria convert nitrates in the soil back into nitrogen gas, which returns to the air.
worked_examples.answer: Denitrifying bacteria release nitrogen gas back to the air.

exercises.question: How do microorganisms help in the nitrogen cycle?
What is nitrogen fixation?
Give one example of a plant that hosts nitrogen-fixing bacteria.

concepts.title: Microorganisms in Industry
concepts.definition: Microorganisms are used in industry to make products such as alcohol, vinegar, antibiotics, enzymes, and biogas through large-scale fermentation.
concepts.key_idea: Industries use microorganisms to produce useful products on a large scale through fermentation.
question_patterns: Name one industrial product made using microorganisms.
How is vinegar produced industrially?
What is biogas and which microorganisms make it?
How are antibiotics produced on a large scale?
Give one example of industrial fermentation.

solution_steps.explain: Note which industrial product is being made, such as alcohol or vinegar.
Name the microorganism involved, such as yeast for alcohol.
Describe how the microorganism produces the product through fermentation.

worked_examples.question: Name one industrial product made using microorganisms.
worked_examples.solution: Alcohol is produced industrially using yeast through fermentation.
worked_examples.answer: Alcohol is made using yeast fermentation.

worked_examples.question: How is vinegar produced industrially?
worked_examples.solution: Vinegar is produced when bacteria convert alcohol into acetic acid.
worked_examples.answer: Bacteria convert alcohol into acetic acid to make vinegar.

worked_examples.question: What is biogas and which microorganisms make it?
worked_examples.solution: Biogas is a fuel made from decaying organic matter by anaerobic bacteria, producing methane.
worked_examples.answer: Biogas is methane made by anaerobic bacteria from organic waste.

exercises.question: How are antibiotics produced on a large scale?
Give one example of industrial fermentation.
Name one enzyme produced using microorganisms.

concepts.title: Counting Microorganism Colonies
concepts.definition: We can count the number of microorganism colonies or cells in a sample to compare growth under different conditions.
concepts.formula: total colonies = colonies from plate A + colonies from plate B
concepts.key_idea: Adding the colonies counted on different plates gives the total number of colonies observed.
question_patterns: A plate has 12 bacterial colonies and another has 18. What is the total number of colonies?
Count the total colonies if three plates have 10, 15, and 20 colonies.
If one plate has 25 colonies and another has 30, what is the total?
Find the total number of colonies given plates with 8 and 14 colonies.
Two plates have 22 and 28 colonies. What is the total?

solution_steps.explain: Write down the number of colonies on each plate.
Sum the colony counts from all plates to get the total.
Check that the total equals the sum of the individual counts.

worked_examples.question: A plate has 12 bacterial colonies and another has 18. What is the total number of colonies?
worked_examples.solution: Add the counts: 12 + 18 = 30.
worked_examples.answer: 30 colonies.

worked_examples.question: Count the total colonies if three plates have 10, 15, and 20 colonies.
worked_examples.solution: Add the counts: 10 + 15 + 20 = 45.
worked_examples.answer: 45 colonies.

worked_examples.question: If one plate has 25 colonies and another has 30, what is the total?
worked_examples.solution: Add the counts: 25 + 30 = 55.
worked_examples.answer: 55 colonies.

exercises.question: Find the total number of colonies given plates with 8 and 14 colonies.
Two plates have 22 and 28 colonies. What is the total?
Three plates have 5, 11, and 19 colonies. Find the total.
